definition: A hash table stores values under keys and finds a key by hashing it to a slot. With a good hash and a moderate load, lookup, insert, and delete average constant time. A run of collisions in one slot degrades that slot toward a linear scan.
details: The load factor is the number of keys divided by the number of slots. Growing the table and rehashing keeps the load factor down.
Keys need a stable hash and an equality test. Mutable keys that change hash after insertion are lost.

complexity.time: Average lookup, insert, and delete are O(1). Worst case is O(n) when many keys land in one slot.
complexity.space: O(n) for the entries, plus the slot array.

examples: A dictionary from user id to account
Counting how many times each word appears
